title: Brewster's Tab
statusNote: Events follow Wikipedia's plot summary of the film. Timestamps follow story order and haven't been checked against subtitles, and most dollar figures are modelled estimates in 1985 dollars.

events.label: Hackensack Bulls
events.detail: Monty Brewster pitches for a minor-league team. He has never earned more than $11,000 a year.
react: Market's closed. So is his wallet.

events.label: Bailed out
events.detail: After a bar fight, a man named Donaldo posts bail for Monty and Spike and takes them to a Manhattan law firm.
react: First expense of the film, and somebody else paid it.

events.label: The will
events.detail: Great-uncle Rupert Horn's terms: spend $30 million in 30 days and inherit $300 million, owning nothing at the end.
react: Thirty million in thirty days. A million a day, weekends included.

events.label: Turns down the wimp clause
events.detail: Monty passes on a guaranteed $1 million and takes the challenge. Angela Drake, a paralegal, is assigned to track his spending.
react: He passed on a sure million. The pit goes quiet.

events.label: Day one walking money
events.detail: New clothes for Monty and Spike, and cash for the month.
react: New suits all round. Tailors up 4% on the day.
daily: Cash for tips and nights out

events.label: Suite at the Plaza
events.detail: An expensive suite at the Plaza Hotel, billed by the night.
react: Billed by the night, so it drips onto the tab every day.

events.label: Office space
events.detail: A Manhattan office on short notice. He can't buy it, so it's rent, plus rented furniture.
react: Leasing, never buying. Smart money, for once.

events.label: Hiring spree
events.detail: He hires personal staff on exorbitant salaries. The will allows it as long as he gets value for their work.
react: Forty new hires. Nobody asked what they'll do.

events.label: Limos and security
events.detail: Cars and guards on call around the clock.
react: Four cars, six guards, one passenger.

events.label: Bad bets
events.detail: He places bad gambling bets. Losses only count up to 5% of the money, $1.5 million.
react: He's backing every long shot on the card.

events.label: Spike invests
events.detail: Spike, who doesn't know the rules, puts some of Monty's money into deals. They're good deals.
react: Spike's picking stocks. Spike is good at picking stocks.

events.label: Spike's deal pays off
events.detail: One of Spike's investments earns money. It comes back and the tab goes down.

events.label: Runs for mayor
events.detail: He puts most of his money into a protest campaign urging New Yorkers to vote for None of the Above.

events.label: Fender-bender payoff
events.detail: After a minor car accident with a businessman, Monty is the one who pays.
react: Whose fault was it? Doesn't matter. Monty pays.

events.label: Ad blitz
events.detail: TV spots and billboards that tell people not to vote for anybody.
react: $6.5 million to tell people not to vote. Worth every cent.
calc: Prime-time TV spots in New York

events.label: Another good deal
events.detail: More money comes back from Spike's investments.

events.label: Settling with the candidates
events.detail: Heller and Salvino, the major candidates, threaten to sue over his rhetoric. He settles out of court for several million dollars.
react: Paying his rivals to drop a lawsuit. Budgeted as 'several million'.

events.label: Rallies and polling
events.detail: The campaign keeps spending while None of the Above climbs in the polls.
react: His numbers are climbing. That's the problem.

events.label: Bulls vs. Yankees
events.detail: He hires the New York Yankees for a three-inning exhibition against the Bulls, with himself pitching.
react: Minor league team, major league invoice.

events.label: The rare stamp
events.detail: He buys a rare stamp at great expense and uses it to mail a postcard to the law firm. Using it for its purpose is allowed.
react: He mailed it. He really mailed it.

events.label: Drops out
events.detail: He's leading in the polls, and the mayor's $60,000 salary would count as an asset under the will. He ends the campaign.
react: Mayor pays $60,000 a year. That's an asset. Hard pass.

events.label: Everything else
events.detail: The plot says the party uses his last $38,000, so anything the itemized estimates miss is already spent by then. It sits here as one entry.
react: Every invoice, every tip, every IOU. Out the door.

events.label: The party after the game
events.detail: He spends his last $38,000 on a party. By the final morning his friends and entourage are gone, and so are the daily costs.

events.label: Money he thought was gone
events.detail: Warren Cox, bribed by the firm's partners, hands Monty money everyone thought was spent. He isn't broke after all.

events.label: Angela's retainer
events.detail: Moments before the deadline, he pays that money to Angela as a retainer for her legal services.
All of the money is spent. He inherits the whole estate.
react: Closing bell. Thirty spent, three hundred banked.
